task: Minimize a TurtleBot 4's world model's held-out prediction error relative to naive baselines ('the reading stays as it is', 'keep the current velocity'), combined as a geometric mean over its prediction heads (lidar sectors, floor speed, wheel odometry, wheel speeds, motor current, IR, pose change) at 0.1, 0.5 and 1 s ahead, on the val slice of each recorded driving session. combined_score is minus the log of that ratio: 0 is level with the baselines, higher is better.

arch.contract: Expose build(input_dim, **params) -> torch.nn.Module with: - z_dim: int, the size of the state; - encode(x): inputs (B, input_dim) -> states (B, z_dim); - rollout(z0, actions): z0 (B, z_dim), actions (B, h, 2) -> states (B, h+1, z_dim), z0 first; - decode(zs, current): states (B, h+1, z_dim) and each target's current reading (B, 1, size) -> {target: (B, h+1, size)}, one entry per dataset.TARGETS name; continuous targets in the standardized units of `current` (predicting a change from it is the baseline's choice, not a requirement), bump and slip as logits; - pose(z0, zs): z0 (B, 1, z_dim) and states (B, h, z_dim) -> pose changes (B, h, 3). The harness scores the model only through these, on held-out windows it never trains on. The driver (train_driver) builds on encode() and z_dim, so keep them meaningful: a state the policy can read. Everything must be differentiable and deterministic given torch's seed.

objective.contract: Expose loss(model, batch) -> (total, parts): total a scalar tensor carrying grad, parts a dict of named scalar tensors (for logging). batch is one standardized training batch from the batcher (dataset.raw_batch's keys, standardized by dataset.Normalizer: inputs (B, h+1, d), actions (B, h, 2), every dataset.TARGETS name (B, h+1, size), pose (B, h+1, 3), and for each sensor <name>_ok (the reading is real) and <name>_seen (the encoder saw it) (B, h+1, 1)). Only real readings (<name>_ok) may count as targets; a reading the encoder didn't see must not seed a prediction (model.current_readings). Selection measures held-out prediction error relative to naive baselines, never this loss, so a loss that is low without predicting well earns nothing.

optim.contract: Expose make(parameters, **params) -> (optimizer, scheduler or None, batch_size). The harness calls optimizer.step() after clipping gradients to norm 10, then scheduler.step() if there is one, every iteration. Training stops when the val error hasn't improved for 2,000 iterations (or at 50,000), so a schedule can't know the number of steps in advance: make it a function of the step count, not of a planned total. batch_size is the number of training windows per step.

batcher.contract: Expose make(sessions, train, norm, rng, batch_size, **params) -> next_batch(), where sessions are dataset.SessionData, train the (session index, window start) pairs of every training window, norm the dataset.Normalizer, rng a numpy Generator seeded by the run's seed. next_batch() returns one batch: a dict of numpy arrays as dataset.window_batch returns them (standardized), with batch_size windows. Use only training windows (train), never val or test ones; draw randomness only from rng, so a run is reproducible from its seed.

registry.jail_notes: Scoring trains one world model per seed with pet_learn.train_world on six recorded driving sessions (about 80 minutes of a person driving the robot around a home with the game controller), until its val error hasn't improved for 2,000 iterations, keeping the best iteration, and measures it on held-out windows: the val slice (80-90% of each session's driving, which also picks the iteration) for selection. Inputs are 88 numbers per 0.1 s step (dataset.inputs: 60 lidar sectors, floor, odometry, wheel speeds, currents, bump sides, slip, stall, the previous command, 7 IR readings, whether the motors have power, and a real-or-missing flag per sensor); the model predicts every reading 1-10 steps ahead from the commands actually sent. Sensors drop out (Wi-Fi loses lidar scans for minutes at a time); missing readings are 0 with their flag off and never count as targets. Training is on the Mac's GPU or a RunPod GPU, a few minutes per seed, so speed matters. You cannot run the real harness from here: write the impl to be correct by construction and state any speed or accuracy claim as unmeasured. The score is relative to baselines that already predict 'nothing changes', so a mechanism earns only by predicting change: how the robot and what it senses move in response to its commands. Keep the model's state (encode, z_dim) meaningful: a driving policy is trained on it afterwards.
